heading: Introduction to Java
title: Introduction to Java
description: Learn the basics of Java programming language

dataList.data: Java is a high-level, object-oriented programming language developed by Sun Microsystems (now Oracle). It's widely used for building enterprise applications, Android apps, web applications, and more. Java's philosophy of 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' makes it platform-independent.

Java was developed by James Gosling and his team at Sun Microsystems in 1995. Originally called Oak, it was designed for interactive television but later evolved into a general-purpose programming language. Java's popularity exploded with the rise of the internet and web applications.

The JVM is the heart of Java's platform independence. Java code is compiled into bytecode, which can run on any device with a JVM installed. This 'compile once, run anywhere' approach is one of Java's biggest strengths.
Java programs are organized into classes. Every Java program must have at least one class with a main method, which serves as the entry point for the program.
This code defines a class with a main method that prints 'Hello, World!' to the console.
Now that you have a basic understanding of Java, explore our sections on data types, control structures, object-oriented programming, and more advanced topics like collections and multithreading.
